name: Noah
charge: Doing according to all that God commanded him
summary: In a world where every imagination of man's heart was only evil continually, one man was just and perfect in his generations and walked with God. He was told to build an ark and did it exactly, and he and his house were the only ones saved through the flood.
offense: Noah found grace in the Lord's eyes, was just and perfect in his generations, and walked with God while the earth was corrupt and filled with violence (Genesis 6:8-13). He was given a work whose form was specified: the ark's material, rooms, covering, dimensions, door, and stories (Genesis 6:14-16). His faith took the shape of carrying out what he had been told. He also had to gather food and bring living creatures into the ark. Genesis 7 distinguishes the clean beasts taken by sevens from the unclean taken by two (Genesis 6:19-22; Genesis 7:2-5). The distinctions were part of the command, not details he was free to discard. Twice the account records that he did according to all the Lord commanded him. Hebrews says he was warned of things not seen as yet and moved with fear to prepare for the saving of his house (Hebrews 11:7). Peter calls him a preacher of righteousness (2 Peter 2:5). Preparation and testimony belonged together: he acted upon the warning instead of waiting for the destruction to prove it true.
judgment: The Lord called Noah's household into the ark and shut him in; Noah and those with him were preserved when the judgment overtook the earth (Genesis 7:1,16,23). His household benefited from a faith expressed in sustained work. Hebrews calls him an heir of the righteousness which is by faith, not merely a survivor of danger. Afterward he built an altar and offered of the clean beasts and fowls. God established the covenant with Noah, his seed, and every living creature, promising that a flood would not again destroy all flesh and setting the bow in the cloud as its token (Genesis 8:20-22; Genesis 9:8-17). The renewed earth also carried commands: replenish it, abstain from blood, and reckon with God's requirement of human life (Genesis 9:1-6). Deliverance opened a continuing duty, not freedom from God's rule.

verses.text: But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.
These are the generations of Noah: Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God.
And God said unto Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me; for the earth is filled with violence through them; and, behold, I will destroy them with the earth.
Make thee an ark of gopher wood; rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and shalt pitch it within and without with pitch.
And this is the fashion which thou shalt make it of: The length of the ark shall be three hundred cubits, the breadth of it fifty cubits, and the height of it thirty cubits.
A window shalt thou make to the ark, and in a cubit shalt thou finish it above; and the door of the ark shalt thou set in the side thereof; with lower, second, and third stories shalt thou make it.
And, behold, I, even I, do bring a flood of waters upon the earth, to destroy all flesh, wherein is the breath of life, from under heaven; and every thing that is in the earth shall die.
But with thee will I establish my covenant; and thou shalt come into the ark, thou, and thy sons, and thy wife, and thy sons’ wives with thee.
And of every living thing of all flesh, two of every sort shalt thou bring into the ark, to keep them alive with thee; they shall be male and female.
Of fowls after their kind, and of cattle after their kind, of every creeping thing of the earth after his kind, two of every sort shall come unto thee, to keep them alive.
And take thou unto thee of all food that is eaten, and thou shalt gather it to thee; and it shall be for food for thee, and for them.
Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he.
And the Lord said unto Noah, Come thou and all thy house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.
And Noah builded an altar unto the Lord; and took of every clean beast, and of every clean fowl, and offered burnt offerings on the altar.

And the Lord smelled a sweet savour; and the Lord said in his heart, I will not again curse the ground any more for man’s sake; for the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth; neither will I again smite any more every thing living, as I have done.
While the earth remaineth, seedtime and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease.
And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth.

And the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth, and upon every fowl of the air, upon all that moveth upon the earth, and upon all the fishes of the sea; into your hand are they delivered.
Every moving thing that liveth shall be meat for you; even as the green herb have I given you all things.
But flesh with the life thereof, which is the blood thereof, shall ye not eat.
And surely your blood of your lives will I require; at the hand of every beast will I require it, and at the hand of man; at the hand of every man’s brother will I require the life of man.
Whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God made he man.
And you, be ye fruitful, and multiply; bring forth abundantly in the earth, and multiply therein.
And God spake unto Noah, and to his sons with him, saying,
And I, behold, I establish my covenant with you, and with your seed after you;
And with every living creature that is with you, of the fowl, of the cattle, and of every beast of the earth with you; from all that go out of the ark, to every beast of the earth.
And I will establish my covenant with you; neither shall all flesh be cut off any more by the waters of a flood; neither shall there any more be a flood to destroy the earth.
And God said, This is the token of the covenant which I make between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for perpetual generations:
I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.
And it shall come to pass, when I bring a cloud over the earth, that the bow shall be seen in the cloud:
And I will remember my covenant, which is between me and you and every living creature of all flesh; and the waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.
And the bow shall be in the cloud; and I will look upon it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is upon the earth.
And God said unto Noah, This is the token of the covenant, which I have established between me and all flesh that is upon the earth.

By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith.
And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly;
Though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they should deliver but their own souls by their righteousness, saith the Lord God.

text.text: And every living substance was destroyed which was upon the face of the ground, both man, and cattle, and the creeping things, and the fowl of the heaven; and they were destroyed from the earth: and Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark.

entries.commentary: The men who began to multiply on the face of the earth were of the other nations; they were not the direct descendants of Adam. The sons of God are the lineage of Adam laid out in chapter 5; that is the distinction between the sons of God and the daughters of men. The law against marrying into the other nations began here in Genesis. It was already known, and Moses had to reiterate that same law to the children of Israel when they came over Jordan.
Here the Most High shortened the lifespan of man to a hundred and twenty years. In chapter 5 the forefathers lived seven, eight, and nine hundred years.

The giants in the earth came from the sons of God intermingling with the other nations, and the children born to them became mighty men of renown. The angels which kept not their first estate are these same men of [Genesis 6:4](/bible/genesis/6#v4); they came from the lineage of Adam, and their first estate was sons of God. Another word for angel is messenger.

Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord; he was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God. Without Noah none of us would be here; Shem, Ham, and Japheth repopulated the earth after the flood.
The ark was a literal boat, made of gopher wood.

At this time the animals were vegetarian; that is why the Most High explained to Noah to gather food for himself, for his family, and for the animals, and why the animals did not eat one another on the ark.

Noah did all that the Most High commanded him by faith. Up to that time rain had never been seen; it takes faith to build an ark for a thing that has never happened. While the ark was preparing, Noah was a preacher of righteousness, telling his people to repent, and the longsuffering of the Most High waited for them to repent. Eight souls were saved by water; the ones that were actually in the water died, so this is not talking about getting baptized. As Noah prepared the ark to the saving of his house, we must prepare our households for when Christ comes back; that takes the same faith. In the days of Noah they were eating, drinking, and marrying until Noah entered the ark and there was no more chance to repent; so shall the coming of the Son of man be. We have to put on the spirit of Noah.

The dietary law was not yet instituted, but the Most High had already defined what was a clean beast and what was an unclean beast, all the way back in Genesis; Moses reiterated that law to the children of Israel. Today this gets confused with the doctrine that says I can eat all things through Christ who strengthens me, and that is not true; the laws were instituted for us to discern between the unclean and the clean. The beasts went in male and female to keep seed alive upon the face of all the earth, so that they could repopulate once the earth dried up; nature itself tells you what we should and should not be doing.

Up until this point it had never rained on the earth; a mist went up from the earth and watered the ground. Understand the faith Noah had to have, being told to build an ark because it was going to rain, a thing that had never happened.

The great deep is the seas, the rivers, and the oceans. The windows of heaven are the sky, the firmament, and their opening is the rain. This is the first time it ever rained on the earth, and when the rain came it came with destruction.

This was the first time the Most High destroyed the earth for the wickedness that was being done. The flood came because they despised the commandments; destruction came because of sin. Of them that dwelt in the world only Noah and his household were left, of whom came all righteous men: through Shem's seed to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and through their line the Israelites. The breath of life is twofold. One is the commandments, which were given to Adam; the other is the breathing life, the oxygen. Here everything on the dry land that breathed died; the fish were not touched.
The windows of heaven being stopped and the rain from heaven being restrained shows you that the windows of heaven refer to the rain.

Noah built an altar and offered burnt offerings of every clean beast and every clean fowl, and the Most High smelled a sweet savour and said He would not again curse the ground any more for man's sake. An everlasting covenant was made with Noah that all flesh should perish no more by a flood. Before it was water; the next time it is going to be fire, so let us get our minds right. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant)
Noah and his sons were told to replenish the earth after the flood, and the earth is replenished with righteous children; a multitude of ungodly children profits nothing.
The fear and dread of man upon the beasts is not how it was in the beginning, and not how it will remain; the original relationship between man and the animals will be restored.

This is the introduction of man eating meat. The Most High did not give man a new stomach; the body was already made for it and it lay dormant until after the flood. Having the liberty to eat meat does not mean eating without balance; be not too greedy upon meats, for excess of meats brings sickness. The law of what may be eaten was already understood; you could not eat everything. The doctrine that says you can pray over anything and eat it is a seducing spirit and a doctrine of devils. Fish is meat; all flesh is not the same flesh, but the flesh of beasts, of fishes, and of birds are all flesh. Every creature of God is good for what it was made for, and it is sanctified by the word of God, and the word that sanctifies what may be eaten is the dietary law.
The law against eating flesh with the blood was given to Adam and is still in place with Noah; the word is true from the beginning.

The Most High requiring blood at the hand of every beast is animal sacrifice, still in place with Noah, passed down generation to generation. The judgment for sin has always been death. When Eve sinned and caused Adam to sin, either they had to die, or something had to stand in their place; the blood of the animal stood in for them. That is the scapegoat: it takes the wrongdoings, mistakes, and faults of others and places them on the animal. That is why Cain and Abel were bringing offerings, because they knew of the sacrifice from [Genesis 3](/bible/genesis/3).

Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed: life for life. This law is way before Moses, so it cannot be dismissed as the law of Moses. The laws were never done away with; Christ came not to destroy the law but to fulfil, and not one jot or tittle passes from the law.

The covenant established here is with Noah, his seed, and every living creature: all flesh shall never again be cut off by the waters of a flood. This is a general covenant with all flesh. The covenant with Israel is found in [Jeremiah 31](/bible/jeremiah/31).

The bow in the cloud, the rainbow, is the token of the covenant between the Most High and the earth; it compasses the heaven about with a glorious circle, and His hands bended it. The world has taken that same bow, the token of the covenant, and turned it into the symbol of sodomy. The spiritual eyes will see what that means: the great city is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt.
The waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh. The next time the destruction is not water but fire, when the day of the Lord comes and the elements melt with fervent heat.

Shem, Ham, and Japheth went forth out of the ark and the whole earth was overspread from them. Ham dwelt in what is called Africa; Shem in the land mass toward Arabia; Japheth went into Europe. Ham is the father of Canaan, and Canaan dwelt in the land later called the land of Israel. That is how you know the land of Israel is a part of Africa; the maps separate Israel from Africa so that the connection is not made.

Noah was still perfect and righteous. A just man falleth seven times and riseth up again; one fall does not undo righteousness. Understand Noah's heart: he preached repentance for around a hundred years, and everyone he knew outside his house drowned. Strong drink is for him that is ready to perish and wine for those of heavy hearts; Noah drank too much, but he remained righteous in the eyes of the Most High. Ham saw the nakedness of his father and did not cover him; Shem and Japheth went backward and covered their father without looking. The commandments concerning nakedness were being applied; [Leviticus 18](/bible/leviticus/18) opens those laws.

Noah was asleep, so how did he know what his younger son had done? The Most High speaks to man in a dream, in a vision of the night, and reveals His secret unto His servants the prophets; Noah was a preacher of righteousness, and the Lord told him. Cursed be Canaan: a servant of servants unto his brethren. Blessed be the Lord God of Shem: it was revealed that the Messiah and the righteous seed would come through Shem.

Certain of the elders of Israel came and sat before Ezekiel, and the word of the Lord said these men have set up their idols in their hearts, setting up something above God, and put the stumbling block of their iniquity before their face. The Most High asks whether He should be inquired of at all by them. Every man of the house of Israel that sets up his idols in his heart and comes to the prophet, the Lord will answer according to the multitude of his idols, that He may take the house of Israel in their own heart, because they are all estranged from Him through their idols and spiritual idolatry.

The Most High tells the house of Israel to repent, come back to His laws, and turn themselves from their idols and away from all their abominations. Every one of the house of Israel, or the stranger that sojourns in Israel, who separates himself from Him and sets up idols in his heart and comes to a prophet to inquire, the Lord will answer by Himself and set His face against that man. He will make him a sign and a proverb, meaning a curse, and cut him off from the midst of His people as an example, that they may know He is the Lord.

If a prophet is deceived when he has spoken a thing, the Lord Himself has deceived that prophet; do not try to deceive yourself in this truth, and when we get counsel we should take it and keep it moving. He will stretch out His hand upon that prophet and destroy him from the midst of His people Israel, and both shall bear the punishment of their iniquity. This is so the house of Israel may go no more astray from Him nor be polluted any more with their transgressions, but be His people and He their God. -

The word of the Lord came saying that when a land sins by trespassing grievously, He will stretch out His hand upon it, break the staff of its bread, and send famine to cut off man and beast. Though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they should deliver but their own souls by their righteousness. No one can save anyone else; it does not matter who you are or what your status is in Israel, you have to save yourself by your own righteousness.

If He causes noisome beasts to pass through the land and spoil it so that it is desolate and no man may pass through, this is one of His judgments. Though these three men were in it, as the Lord lives they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters; they only shall be delivered by their righteousness, but the land shall be desolate.

If He brings a sword upon that land to cut off man and beast, though these three men were in it, they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters. They only shall deliver themselves by their righteousness.

If He sends a pestilence into the land and pours out His fury upon it in blood to cut off man and beast, though Noah, Daniel, and Job were in it, they shall deliver neither son nor daughter. They shall but deliver their own souls by their righteousness; everyone has to work out their own righteousness in fear and trembling, delivering their own soul by keeping the Most High's commandments. -

How much more when the Most High sends His four sore judgments upon Jerusalem, the sword, the famine, the noisome beast, and the pestilence, to cut off man and beast; and these are not just for back then but for today. Behold, a remnant shall be left, both sons and daughters, that shall be brought forth unto you, and you shall see their ways and their doings. You shall be comforted concerning the evil the Most High brought upon Jerusalem when you see their ways, and you shall know He has not done without cause all that He has done in it. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry)
